claim: Endpoints of a standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator can be Network Load Balancers, Application Load Balancers, EC2 instances or Elastic IP addresses; the accelerator's static IP addresses are the single point of contact for clients.
question: Which load balancer types can be endpoints of a Global Accelerator standard accelerator?

values.display: Network Load Balancers, Application Load Balancers
a single point of contact for clients

evidence.quote: Endpoints for standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator can be Network Load Balancers, Application Load Balancers, Amazon EC2 instances, or Elastic IP addresses.

In AWS Global Accelerator, static IP addresses serve as a single point of contact for clients, and, with a standard accelerator, Global Accelerator distributes incoming traffic across healthy endpoints.

claim: With host conditions, one Application Load Balancer can route requests for multiple domains, based on the host field in the HTTP header.
question: How can one Application Load Balancer serve several domains?

evidence.quote: You can configure rules for your listener that forward requests based on the host field in the HTTP header.
This enables you to route requests to multiple domains using a single load balancer.

claim: With path conditions, an Application Load Balancer forwards requests based on the URL, so you can split an application into smaller services and route each request to the correct service.
question: How does an Application Load Balancer route requests to different services of one application?

values.display: forward requests based on the URL
structure your application as smaller services

evidence.quote: You can configure rules for your listener that forward requests based on the URL in the request.
This enables you to structure your application as smaller services, and route requests to the correct service based on the content of the URL.

claim: An Application Load Balancer can route to multiple applications on one EC2 instance: you register the instance or IP address with several target groups, each on a different port.
question: How can one Application Load Balancer reach several applications that run on the same instance?

evidence.quote: You can register an instance or IP address with multiple target groups, each on a different port.

claim: An Application Load Balancer is charged for each hour or partial hour that it is running, and each partial hour is billed as a full hour, plus the Load Balancer Capacity Units (LCU) it uses.
question: Does an Application Load Balancer bill per hour even when little traffic flows, and how is a partial hour billed?

evidence.quote: You are charged for each hour or partial hour that an Application Load Balancer is running.
Each partial Application Load Balancer hour used is billed as a full hour.
You are also charged for the number of Load Balancer Capacity Units (LCU) used per minute.

claim: A Network Load Balancer and a Gateway Load Balancer are each charged for every hour or partial hour they run, with each partial hour billed as a full hour, plus the capacity units they use (NLCU or GLCU).
question: How are Network Load Balancers and Gateway Load Balancers billed for running time?

qualifiers.scope: per Network Load Balancer or Gateway Load Balancer

evidence.quote: You are charged for each hour or partial hour that a Network Load Balancer is running.
Each partial Network Load Balancer hour used is billed as a full hour.
You are charged for each hour or partial hour that a Gateway Load Balancer is running.
You are also charged for the number of Network Load Balancer Capacity Units (NLCU) used by Network Load Balancer per minute.
You are also charged for the number of Gateway Load Balancer Capacity Units (GLCU) used by Gateway Load Balancer per minute.

claim: For an Application Load Balancer with 10 or fewer rules, the rule evaluations dimension is ignored in the LCU calculation, so many routing rules on one load balancer only add cost above 10 rules.
question: When does the number of listener rules start to add LCU cost on an Application Load Balancer?

qualifiers.scope: per Application Load Balancer, LCU rule evaluations dimension
qualifiers.condition: rules configured on the load balancer

evidence.quote: Note 2: If you have 10 or fewer rules configured, the rule evaluations dimension is ignored in LCU computation.

claim: On top of the load balancer charges, you pay standard AWS data transfer charges and standard public IPv4 address charges for all addresses your load balancers consume.
question: Which charges come on top of the Elastic Load Balancing hourly and capacity unit charges?

evidence.quote: You will incur standard AWS data transfer charges, in addition to any ELB charges.
You will incur standard public IPv4 address charges for all the addresses you consume with load balancers.

claim: The Gateway Load Balancer endpoint (GWLBE), a VPC endpoint type powered by AWS PrivateLink, is priced and billed separately from the Gateway Load Balancer.
question: Is the Gateway Load Balancer endpoint included in the Gateway Load Balancer price?

values.display: GWLBE is priced and billed separately

evidence.quote: GWLBE is priced and billed separately.

claim: You are not charged for traffic that the inbound security group rules of a Network Load Balancer block.
question: Do you pay for traffic that a Network Load Balancer security group blocks?

values.display: You are not charged for traffic
blocked by inbound security group rules

evidence.quote: You are not charged for traffic that is blocked by inbound security group rules.

claim: You can associate security groups with a Network Load Balancer only when you create it; if you create it without security groups, you cannot add them later, so AWS recommends adding one at creation.
question: Can you add a security group to an existing Network Load Balancer that was created without one?

values.display: can't associate them with the Network Load Balancer
We recommend that you associate a security group

evidence.quote: If you create a Network Load Balancer without associating any security groups, you can't associate them with the Network Load Balancer later on.
We recommend that you associate a security group with your Network Load Balancer when you create it.

claim: If a Network Load Balancer has no security group, all client traffic can reach its listeners and all traffic can leave it.
question: What traffic can reach a Network Load Balancer that has no security group?

values.display: all traffic can leave the Network Load Balancer

qualifiers.scope: Network Load Balancer without a security group

evidence.quote: If you don't assign a security group to your Network Load Balancer, all client traffic can reach the Network Load Balancer listeners and all traffic can leave the Network Load Balancer.

claim: If the target security groups allow traffic only from the security group of the Network Load Balancer, clients can reach the targets through the load balancer but not directly.
question: How do you stop clients from bypassing a Network Load Balancer and reaching its targets directly?

values.display: prevents them from sending traffic directly

qualifiers.scope: Network Load Balancer and its targets

evidence.quote: You can add a rule to the security groups associated with your targets that references the security group associated with your Network Load Balancer. This allows clients to send traffic to your targets through your Network Load Balancer, but prevents them from sending traffic directly to your targets.
